purpose: Add eight source-exact Frances Ridley Havergal devotional excerpts for Christ's kingship, consecration, service, fellowship, and contentment.

defaults.author: Frances Ridley Havergal
defaults.sourceTitle: My King; or, Daily Thoughts for the King's Children
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1876 A. D. F. Randolph edition is public domain; every excerpt is verified against the stored Library of Congress OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.

entries.title: He Himself Is Our King
entries.text: How glad we are that He Himself is our King!
entries.slideText: How glad we are that He Himself is our King!
entries.sourceLocator: The Promise of the King, page 13
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed devotional sentence when introducing the joy and security of Christ's rule.
entries.reviewNote: This sentence is devotional prose, not Scripture. Establish Christ's kingship from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: The Government into His Hands
entries.text: We are so glad to take Him at His word, and give up the government into His hands
entries.slideText: give up the government into His hands
entries.sourceLocator: The Promise of the King, page 13
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed transition from self-rule to trusting Christ's wise government.
entries.reviewNote: Avoid passive fatalism; surrender to Christ expresses itself in active obedience to his word.

entries.title: My King This Day
entries.text: Lord, be Thou my King this day ! Reign more absolutely in me than ever before.
entries.slideText: Lord, be Thou my King this day !
entries.sourceLocator: The Promise of the King, page 14
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed daily prayer for Christ's rule in the believer's life.
entries.reviewNote: This devotional prayer is not Scripture. Explain Christ's kingship and the believer's obedience from the cited KJV texts.

entries.title: A Life of Victory and Peace
entries.text: What a glorious life of victory and peace opens before us when this is done !
entries.slideText: a glorious life of victory and peace
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed summary after teaching the believer's peace and victory through Christ.
entries.reviewNote: Do not promise freedom from hardship. Define peace and victory from the cited KJV passages and their context.

entries.title: Commune with Him Now
entries.text: Commune with Him now of all that is in your heart
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed invitation to honest prayer and fellowship with the Lord.
entries.reviewNote: Explain communion as prayerful trust grounded in Scripture, not new revelation or mystical impressions.

entries.title: Life Filled with Bright Interests
entries.text: Life is filled with bright interests, time is filled with happy work or peaceful waiting
entries.sourceLocator: Full Satisfaction in the King, page 31
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed contrast between faithful work and patient waiting in a Christ-centered life.
entries.reviewNote: Do not minimize grief or illness. Apply contentment and waiting with pastoral sensitivity from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: The Joy of Willing Consecration
entries.sourceLocator: The Joy of the King, page 61
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed devotional observation after teaching willing service and consecration.
entries.reviewNote: Consecration does not earn salvation. Present it as the glad response of the redeemed to God's mercy.

entries.title: Never Delay the King's Business
entries.text: Especially in that part of it which is between Himself and ourselves alone, let us never delay.
entries.sourceLocator: The Business of the King, page 67
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed appeal against delay in personal obedience and dealings with the Lord.
entries.reviewNote: Apply urgency through the cited KJV passages without pressuring listeners into an emotional or uninformed decision.
